DIAGNOSIS READY: Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension (Pseudotumor Cerebri).

The patient is a 69-year-old woman with hypertension presenting with a 3-week history of headache and worsening vision. Initial workup including blood pressure readings and non-contrast CT head has shown normal results, ruling out hemorrhage, mass effect, and acute vascular events. The clinical picture of raised intracranial pressure signs (presumed papilledema on ophthalmoscopy) without an identifiable structural cause on imaging is most consistent with this diagnosis. I will now request MRI brain with and without contrast to definitively rule out a small posterior fossa mass or venous sinus thrombosis before finalizing the plan.
